title: Your friend is “stuck at immigration”
scenario: A friend studying abroad messages that immigration officers are holding their passport and they need you to pay a “release fee” to a third party. The account contains years of your real conversations.

answers.A: Contact the friend through another channel and, if necessary, verify with their family, university or consulate before sending money.
answers.B: Ask for the name of the authority and case details, then verify them independently.
answers.C: Pay because the long message history proves the account belongs to your friend.

explanation: A compromised account includes all the old history that makes the emergency believable.
proTip: Chat history proves the account had a past—not who controls it now.
